title: Regression Diagnostics: read the evidence behind the results
description: Open the diagnostic files produced by a real example-screen analysis, distinguish design warnings from permutation results, and recognize the limits of a short demonstration run.
objectives: Open Diagnostics inside Regression and verify the output folder being inspected.
Interpret design identifiability, guide support and inference panels in the context of the selected analysis.
Recognize missing fitted-residual panels and limited permutation resolution without inventing a model fit.
prerequisite: Complete the Regression example using its four downloadable score/count pairs. This recording inspects a bounded nonparametric run with 199 permutations, a minimum of two wells, and both guide and gene results. It demonstrates the software and diagnostic interpretation, not final discovery-quality inference.

scenes.narration: Inside Regression, hover over Diagnostics and open it after an analysis has completed. This button reads saved output; it does not fit another model. It opens the newest diagnostics folder found in the project, so verify the path when several runs exist.

The system file manager shows the actual files from our downloaded example-screen analysis. Here the figure preference was PNG. The folder contains design identifiability, design diagnostics, inference diagnostics, a summary table, and a table of collinear guide pairs.

The design has six hundred and six wells, seven hundred and ninety-three parameters, and rank five hundred and ninety-nine. It cannot identify a unique simultaneous coefficient for every guide. This warning explains why we used a permutation analysis; it does not mean a simultaneous model was fitted successfully.

Guide support is uneven: three hundred and fifty-five guides occur in just one well in this design. Sparse support limits what the experiment can establish. Inspect coverage before interpreting effects, and distinguish the full design from the filtered family of guides actually tested.

The design panel helps locate poor support and dependencies between guide predictors. Guides that always occur together are hard to distinguish statistically. Use the collinear-pairs table to inspect specific pairs rather than treating a warning badge as a complete explanation.

The inference panel summarizes four hundred and thirty-four guide tests: their p-value distribution, comparison with a uniform null, and discoveries across adjusted thresholds. This short run has no discoveries at the displayed threshold. A calibration warning is a prompt to investigate, not proof of biological effects.

We used only one hundred and ninety-nine permutations to keep the demonstration short. The minimum attainable empirical p-value is therefore zero point zero zero five. That resolution can be inadequate after multiple-testing correction; use an appropriately planned permutation count for the real analysis.

There is no fitted-residual panel for this permutation run because it did not fit the simultaneous regression model. The p-value comparison we just viewed is not a residual diagnostic. Other analysis modes can write residual panels when they supply observed and fitted values.

The summary records individual panel assessments and the worst assessment for the suite. Read each assessment in context rather than interpreting the overall badge as a software error. The Python regression diagnostics API writes the same kinds of panels from the inputs it is given.

Return to Regression to investigate the inputs or change an analysis choice deliberately. A change needs a new run and new diagnostics; opening this folder never updates old results. Use the Regression tutorial for the full dataset, console, interactive results, and assistance workflow.
